opening_message:
Ticket 1: John Rodriguez (employee ID E049) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E049.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: John Rodriguez (E049) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write (admin requires owning role, which is Engineer). Grant write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows John Rodriguez (E049) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds max; recommend granting read.
reason: The two notes conflict: HR lists John Rodriguez (E049) as full-time (max write for Source Code), while Security lists him as a contractor with basic training (max read for Source Code, write requires advanced training). Given the conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive reading: as a contractor with basic training, write exceeds the maximum, so grant read. Read is within policy under either interpretation and is the safe level.
